name: SANS Internet Storm Center / DShield API
tier_rationale: Established security non-profit/academic operator with a published API page and licence (A8 BR2 names SANS ISC as trusted; P151 chair rationale: 'SANS: tier trusted').

reliability.justification: DShield sensor reports are real firewall-log submissions of opportunistic scanning (not targeted activity); threat-feed memberships re-publish third-party lists and are context, not verdicts.

api.title: SANS ISC API (GET /api/ip/{ip}?json, /api/asnum/{count}/{asn}?json, /api/threatcategory/research?json)

terms.quote: Data is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. 'It is ok to use this data for commercial purposes, for example to protect your own company's network. But again: do not resell' (ISC API page, fetched 2026-11-26).

api.notes: A1 initial class 'noncommercial' (SANS ISC). Off under the corporate profile until licence-cleared: legal records a licence_allow entry for sans_isc.api (basis terms_clause) citing the API page clause, scope 'defence of the company's own networks only, no resale, no inclusion in paid deliverables to third parties' (P151 cond 1-2, day-1 queue). ISC asks API users to identify themselves: the provider profile sends the contact UA (setting contact_email, a team role mailbox), else SKIPPED config. Without Accept: application/json and ?json ISC answers XML or redirects to /blockme.html (BLOCKED challenge, circuit for the run). Attribution: 'SANS ISC / DShield'.
api.licensed_alternative: A licence_allow entry for sans_isc.api quoting the API page's own-network-protection clause (no resale).

notes: Owned by batch p2-G02-3 (P151). No published rate limit ('at times of high load, you may get 429 responses. Please stop sending queries for 5 minutes'): politeness is min_interval 2 s, one connection, no retries, and the core blockme circuit. HTML pages (ipinfo, threatfeeds) redirect scripts to /blockme.html: manual links only.
